description: The US Environmental Protection Agency Plumbing Volume Estimator Tool calculates the water volume associated with different plumbing materials along a selected route through a home or building. Users describe the pipe sections and materials to produce a plumbing map, for example between a faucet and the water main. The results support lead-sampling design and decisions about the volume of stagnant water to flush. This is a building-specific calculation with user-supplied geometry, not a national inventory or a prediction of measured lead concentrations. EPA provides an Excel workbook in macro-enabled and macro-free forms, with an October 2024 guidebook. The documented design environment is Microsoft 365, 64-bit, on Windows 11 Enterprise; compatibility elsewhere was not tested in this review. The public workbook and repository are accessible without a stated charge, but a reuse licence was not established from the inspected documentation. It can prepare plumbing-volume inputs for water-quality studies. EPANET is a related network model, without a claimed direct interface. Workbooks were not downloaded.
